positions.name: ConversationalProvenanceDataModel
positions.frame: How does modeling organizational conversation with append-only provenance differ from traditional entity-fact knowledge graphs?
positions.why: Tanya articulates the architectural foundation of the V2 ontology: the system models live conversations and decision moments with full provenance and zero data retention in GitHub repositories, performing entity and authority disambiguation at generation time rather than pre-computing static entity facts.

positions.name: IntermediaryNetworkEffectsFederation
positions.frame: How can cross-organizational graph federation and intermediary network effects protect against commodity AI transcription and incumbent displacement?
positions.why: Xavier argues that point-solution transcription tools (Fireflies, Otter) will inevitably commoditize and that durability requires becoming an un-disintermediable intermediary like a telephone company; Tanya and Xavier explore how federating private conversational graphs across organizational boundaries creates bilateral network lock-in.

positions.name: StagedFundraisingProcessMarketplace
positions.frame: How should early-stage founders stage fundraising rounds and orchestrate competitive investor momentum rather than seeking individual checks?
positions.why: Xavier advises Tanya on conducting an institutional venture round as a time-bound marketplace rather than sequential asks, prescribing an initial advice-gathering phase to build conviction, reserving high-leverage champions like Emery Park until a term sheet exists, and asserting power through process discipline.

positions.name: EnterprisePilotContractTiering
positions.frame: How should pricing and contract structures scale from team self-service to automated enterprise meeting ingestion?
positions.why: Tanya details the commercial packaging shift from $400/month team plans to $4k+/month enterprise packages driven by pilot feedback demanding automated meeting ingestion, citing her current enterprise pilot moving from an $800/month trial to a $6,000/month MSA in legal review.
